glossary.definition: The mean duration of a shot in a cut piece of film; commercial-cinema ASL fell from ~8-11s pre-1960 to ~4-6s in recent decades per Bordwell's 'intensified continuity', with Barry Salt measuring ~11s to ~7s over 1958-1975 [FACT/excerpt]. The owner's 3-6s stitched-clip format sits faster than that baseline, near trailer/music-video cutting rate [FACT by comparison].

Aligning cuts and visual changes to the track's beats so picture and audio read as one processed stream; practice is to mark beats first (tap-markers or waveform spikes) then conform cuts to the markers, cutting major shot changes on downbeats/accents and leaving minor motion for off-beats [FACT/excerpt].

A priority order for what a cut must preserve when it cannot satisfy everything: Emotion 51%, Story 23%, Rhythm 10%, Eye-trace 7%, two-dimensional plane of screen 5%, three-dimensional space of action 4%; sacrifice from the bottom of the list up, never give up emotion first [FACT/excerpt — Murch, In the Blink of an Eye, as summarized by secondary sources].

Split-edit sound bridges named for the clip shape on the timeline: J-cut = the next clip's audio starts before its picture (audio leads); L-cut = the current clip's audio continues over the next clip's picture (audio trails) [FACT/excerpt].

Gradually varying playback speed inside a clip via a keyframed speed curve, typically normal → slow-motion at the action peak → accelerate out; smoothness depends on source frame rate, so slowing a low-fps AI clip too far needs optical-flow interpolation and risks exposing AI artifacts [FACT/excerpt + ESTIMATE].

An edit where the last frame flows into the first so the restart isn't registered; the editorial technique is to zoom 200-400% on the boundary frames and trim by single frames until they match, with a duplicate-tail-plus-cross-dissolve fallback [FACT/excerpt]. Loops raise rewatches and total watch time, both ranking-relevant signals.

Making a cut's seam disappear by matching the direction, speed, and screen-position of the dominant moving element across the two clips, plus close luminance/hue at the boundary frames [FACT/excerpt].

A transition where a passing occluder's silhouette wipes the frame to reveal the next scene, executed by keyframing a mask along the occluder's edge with the next clip on the track beneath; when the occluder fully covers the frame the technique degenerates to a plain invisible cut needing no mask [FACT/excerpt].

Invisible cut: the outgoing and incoming clips' boundary frames are made identical (commonly both full black) so the cut point cannot be located. Flash frame: a 1-3 frame overexposed/white insert at the cut, often with a flash SFX, that masks the discontinuity with high energy; kept to ≤2 per reel to avoid reading as strobing and to respect photosensitivity [FACT/excerpt + ESTIMATE].

A transition that joins two shots via matching composition or action (e.g. a round glass rim to a round wheel rim); the most 'premium'-reading transition when both boundary frames are deliberately designed for it upstream [FACT/excerpt on definition].

The synthesis decision that composes shot-count budget, sequencing, transitions, and modulated shot length into a 15-60s reel whose energy visibly rises toward a peak (accelerating clip lengths, more assertive transitions) rather than running at a flat rhythm throughout [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the cited pacing/sequencing craft].

nodes.definition: Establish the pacing baseline the whole KB reasons against. Commercial-cinema average shot length (ASL) fell from roughly 8-11 seconds pre-1960 to roughly 4-6 seconds in recent decades — Bordwell's 'intensified continuity'; Barry Salt separately measured a drop from about 11s to about 7s over 1958-1975 [FACT/excerpt — Bordwell PDF + Cinemetrics/Wide Screen discussions]. The owner's stitched-reel format (3/4/5/6 s AI clips) already cuts faster than that cinema baseline, sitting closer to trailer/music-video cutting rate [FACT — arithmetic comparison]. Retention economics compound this: up to roughly 50% of viewers drop off within the first 3 seconds, and watch-time (total seconds, % completed, rewatches) is treated as the dominant ranking signal; a third-party analytics claim that reels holding above ~60% at 3 seconds strongly outperform those below ~40% is carried as [FACT/excerpt], while a separate '5-10x reach' multiplier attached to the same claim is marked [ESTIMATE, medium-low confidence] because it is not a Meta-published number. Together these two curves — cinema's own historical acceleration, and this format's even faster retention-driven baseline — are what every downstream pacing, sequencing and transition decision in this KB is calibrated against.

nodes.definition: Specify how shot length should vary across the reel rather than sit at a metronomic constant. Hold the hero or luxury-reveal shot longest (4-6s), and use shorter 2-3s connective shots between reveals [ESTIMATE — standard editorial craft, high confidence]. Around a structural peak (a music drop, a reveal), accelerate clip lengths on the way in to build tension and decelerate after it to give a sense of arrival. This modulation is what keeps a reel from feeling like a uniform slideshow of equal-length clips even when every source clip is generated at a similar 3-6s duration — the EDIT decides which clips get trimmed shorter and which run closer to full length.

nodes.definition: Fix the mechanical practice of locking cuts to the music. Beat-sync means aligning cuts, transitions and visual changes to beats of the track so that when a cut lands on a drum hit or bass drop the edit reads as intentional and rhythmic, with audio and visual processed as one coherent stream [FACT/excerpt]. Do NOT cut on every single beat — that reads frantic; instead cut major shot changes on downbeats/accents and let minor motion (a speed ramp, a camera land) carry the off-beats [FACT/excerpt]. Mechanically: mark beats first — tap-markers in CapCut/VN, waveform spikes in Premiere/Resolve, or automatic beat detection — then conform the cuts to those markers, i.e. audio is locked before picture [FACT/excerpt]. A frequently repeated claim that Facebook found strongly-synced audio-visual reels see 'up to 40% higher completion' circulates across these guides but its original source could not be located or fetched, so it is held [UNKNOWN provenance] and must never be cited as verified fact.

nodes.definition: Establish the classic shot-size sequencing logic and its application to a 3-6s-clip reel. Coverage is planned wide (establishes geography) -> medium (carries action/relationship) -> close (delivers emotion); alternating sizes creates the scene's rhythm, with quick cuts between close-ups and action building intensity and steadier wides/mediums calming it [FACT/excerpt]. Two adjacent shots should differ meaningfully in size or angle to avoid a jump cut (the classic '30-degree rule' avoidance) [ESTIMATE — canonical continuity craft, high confidence]. Because a viewer cannot rescan a 3s shot the way they can a longer take, eye-trace continuity matters more here than in slower media: place the next shot's subject where the previous shot left the viewer's eye — e.g. a persona exiting frame-right at eye-level should be met by the next clip's subject entering at that same screen position [ESTIMATE — direct application of Murch's eye-trace criterion, high confidence].

nodes.definition: Fix Walter Murch's Rule of Six as the tie-breaker for what a cut may sacrifice when constraints conflict. Priority order for any cut: Emotion 51%, Story 23%, Rhythm 10%, Eye-trace 7%, two-dimensional plane of screen 5%, three-dimensional space of action 4%; sacrifice from the bottom up, never give up emotion [FACT/excerpt — Murch, In the Blink of an Eye, summarized by secondary craft sources]. This ranking is the explicit authority this KB cites whenever a beat-lock, a shot-size rule, or a transition trick would otherwise force an editor to choose between competing goods: rhythm (10%) is subordinate to emotion (51%) and story (23%), so a perfectly on-beat cut that lands on the wrong emotional beat should still be moved.

nodes.definition: Define and apply J-cut/L-cut sound bridging on a pipeline where clips arrive with no production audio. nodes.definition: Fix the editorial (timeline-trim) technique for a seamless loop, as distinct from the AI-native generation trick the sibling cover/shot-analysis KB owns. nodes.definition: Compose the whole KB into the final assembly decision: build a 15-60s reel whose energy visibly rises toward a peak rather than running at a flat rhythm throughout [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the cited pacing/sequencing craft]. Reconciled assembly rules: (1) spend the CLIP_COUNT_BUDGET_BY_DURATION ceiling deliberately, never padding to fill it; (2) inherit only QC'd transition material per TRANSITION_MATERIAL_HANDOFF, escalating a failed pair for regeneration rather than patching around it; (3) let clip lengths accelerate toward the reel's structural peak and decelerate after it per SHOT_LENGTH_MODULATION, with the highest-effort transitions (whip, wipe, flash, match cut) reserved for that peak per TRANSITION_INVENTORY_SELECTION; (4) close on a LOOP_CONSTRUCTION_EDIT_TECHNIQUE-matched pair only when the reel is designed for rewatch value, not mid-escalation; (5) keep every cut inside the MOBILE_TIMELINE_FRAMING safe zones and the SOUND_OFF_FIRST_TOUCH_DESIGN hook constraint throughout; (6) run the whole assembly through the EDITOR_TOOL_HYBRID_WORKFLOW pipeline (mobile beat-lock, desktop finish) before handing off to color grading. A reel that hits its shot-count budget and its transition inventory correctly but never actually rises in energy toward a peak has satisfied the craft checklist without satisfying the assembly's actual goal.

included: the six reconciled assembly rules (budget discipline, QC'd-material-only, accelerate/decelerate around a peak, loop-only-when-rewatch-designed, safe-zone/hook compliance, tool-pipeline sequencing)
the explicit goal of a rising-energy curve, not just a checklist pass
excluded: the color-grading and delivery step this assembly hands off to (owned by kb_color_grading)

edges.why_related: locking every major cut to the beat can force a cut away from the reel's actual emotional peak, and Murch ranks rhythm at only 10% against emotion's 51%
edges.resolution_rule: when a strict beat-lock would land a cut off the emotional peak, slip the cut by a frame or two to the nearest strong beat rather than sacrificing the emotional moment

edges.why_related: a seamless loop wants a soft, decelerating return for an unnoticed restart, while an escalation-energy assembly wants sustained rising energy through the very last frame

edges.why_related: both are post-only techniques that disguise a cut's seam using motion/occlusion material rather than a straight cut, executed identically regardless of whether the AI clip supplied clean or imperfect source material

conflict_axes.name: hook_first_vs_classic_wide_establishing_order
conflict_axes.description: Retention economics demand the single strongest image open the reel with no intro, while classic film coverage plans wide-establish first; the two orderings directly conflict for a sub-15-second reel.
poles: open on the strongest hook image
establish geography with a wide shot first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: invert classic order: hook first, establish second, as the five-shot skeleton does

conflict_axes.name: beat_lock_vs_emotion_first_priority
conflict_axes.description: Cut-on-beat practice wants major cuts locked to musical accents, while Murch's Rule of Six ranks rhythm at only 10% below emotion's 51%, so a perfectly on-beat cut can still be the wrong cut.
poles: lock every major cut to the beat
protect the emotional peak even off-beat
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: slip a cut by a frame or two toward the nearest strong beat rather than sacrificing the emotional moment

conflict_axes.name: loop_softness_vs_escalation_energy
conflict_axes.description: A seamless loop wants a decelerating, unnoticed return to the first frame, while an escalation-energy assembly wants clip lengths and intensity rising through the very last frame.
poles: sustained rising energy to the end
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reserve full loop endings for rewatch-designed reels; loop the arrival moment itself on hard-escalation reels

conflict_axes.name: ai_clean_motion_vs_faked_analog_blur
conflict_axes.description: AI-generated whips and fast motion often render too clean, lacking the real optical blur a physical camera would produce, which the whip-blur bridge must fake in post to sell as one continuous move.
poles: accept the AI clip's clean rendered motion as-is
add synthetic blur/zoom to fake analog camera motion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add 2-4 frames of directional blur plus a 5-10% zoom ramp only when the native motion is visibly too clean, not by default on every clip

conflict_axes.name: flash_energy_vs_photosensitivity_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: The flash frame's high-energy paparazzi connotation is easy to overuse, but rapid full-frame flashing risks photosensitivity and, past roughly two per reel, reads as strobing.
poles: cap flashes for accessibility and to avoid strobing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hard-cap flash-frame inserts at roughly two per reel regardless of how many structural beats seem to call for one

conflict_axes.name: hard_cut_default_vs_premium_match_cut_opportunity
conflict_axes.description: Defaulting every transition to the cheap, workhorse hard-cut-on-beat can waste a boundary-frame pair that was deliberately designed upstream for a premium match cut.
poles: default to hard cut on beat everywhere
spend the premium match-cut technique when frames were designed for it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: check the upstream frame-pairing intent before defaulting to a hard cut on a pair designed for a match cut

conflict_axes.name: regenerate_discipline_vs_schedule_pressure
conflict_axes.description: Sending a failed boundary-frame pair back for stills-stage regeneration is the cheapest fix, but schedule pressure tempts patching it with an editing trick instead.
poles: always regenerate a failed pair before video generation
patch a failed pair with extra blur/crop/flash to save time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never substitute an editing trick for a failed upstream QC gate; the round-trip delay is cheaper than the video-generation cost of shipping a bad pair

conflict_axes.name: picture_only_hook_vs_strong_audio_cue
conflict_axes.description: Designing every hook to work fully sound-off can under-use a genuinely strong audio cue (a signature SFX or track intro) that could have anchored the opening.
poles: design the hook to work with sound off entirely
lean on a strong opening audio cue
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the picture-only requirement as the floor, but layer a strong audio cue on top for viewers who do have sound on rather than omitting it

conflict_axes.name: mobile_speed_vs_desktop_precision
conflict_axes.description: Mobile-first editors are fastest for beat-marking and quick assembly, but this KB's frame-accurate techniques (vector matching, single-frame loop trims, mask keyframing) need desktop-level precision.
poles: stay in a fast mobile-first editor
move to a desktop NLE for frame-accurate work
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the mobile editor only for beat-marking and rough assembly, then hand off to a desktop NLE for every technique in this KB that needs frame-level control

edge_cases.description: A reel is padded to the top of its shot-count budget with a weak filler shot purely to hit the ceiling
edge_cases.trigger: an editor treats the CLIP_COUNT_BUDGET_BY_DURATION range as a quota to fill rather than a ceiling
edge_cases.mitigation: spend the budget deliberately; ship a reel at the low end of the range if that is all the strong material supports

edge_cases.description: The single strongest asset is opened on the hook, leaving nothing stronger to escalate toward later in the reel
edge_cases.trigger: front-loading the best shot with no plan for what the escalation curve peaks on instead
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve a second-strongest asset as the escalation peak distinct from the opening hook, so the reel still has somewhere to build to

edge_cases.description: An edit cuts on every single beat of an up-tempo track, producing a frantic rather than intentional rhythm
edge_cases.trigger: conforming cuts to every marker instead of only downbeats/accents
edge_cases.mitigation: cut major shot changes only on downbeats/accents and let minor motion (a ramp, a camera land) carry off-beats

edge_cases.description: An edit cites the unverified 'Facebook 40% higher completion' sync statistic as a justification for aggressive beat-locking
edge_cases.trigger: the UNKNOWN-provenance claim is quoted as verified fact
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the claim only as unverified/UNKNOWN provenance and justify beat-sync decisions from the sourced mark-then-conform practice instead

edge_cases.description: Two adjacent shots of nearly the same size and angle are cut back to back, reading as an unintentional jump cut
edge_cases.trigger: the SHOT_SIZE_RHYTHM meaningful-difference rule is skipped when selecting adjacent takes
edge_cases.mitigation: verify size/angle difference between every adjacent pair before cutting, or insert a connective shot of a different size between them

edge_cases.description: A slow-motion ramp is pushed past the point the source AI clip's fps can smoothly support, exposing morphing artifacts in the interpolated frames
edge_cases.trigger: ramping a 24-30fps AI clip below roughly 50-60% playback speed
edge_cases.mitigation: keep ramps above the ~50-60% floor for AI clips until per-model generated fps is confirmed on the MCP surface, and preview interpolated frames at full resolution before committing

edge_cases.description: A loop's boundary frames cannot be trimmed to a clean pixel match, and the visible seam breaks the illusion of continuity
edge_cases.trigger: the source stills were not designed to match and the 200-400% zoom trim finds no clean alignment
edge_cases.mitigation: fall back to duplicating the first ~1s of footage at the tail and hiding the joint with a 0.5-1s cross-dissolve

edge_cases.description: A whip-blur cut is butt-joined between two clips whose motion vectors do not actually agree, so the seam remains visible despite added blur
edge_cases.trigger: skipping the MOTION_VECTOR_MATCHING checklist before applying the whip-blur recipe
edge_cases.mitigation: verify vector direction and pixel velocity match first; synthetic blur disguises a seam only when the underlying motion already roughly agrees

edge_cases.description: A reel inserts a flash frame at every major cut in an escalation sequence, producing a strobing effect
edge_cases.mitigation: hard-cap flash-frame inserts at two per reel and reserve them for the single highest-energy structural beat

edge_cases.description: A boundary-frame pair fails the upstream shot-analysis QC gate but the editor patches around it with extra blur and a tighter crop instead of escalating for regeneration
edge_cases.trigger: schedule pressure tempts a patch instead of a stills-stage regeneration round-trip
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the pair back to the stills stage for regeneration; stills are the cheap place to fail on a credit-based generation platform, video is not

edge_cases.description: A reel's caption or persona framing lands inside the estimated mobile UI safe-zone bands and is covered by the app's overlay when actually viewed in-app
edge_cases.trigger: trusting the estimated (not officially confirmed) safe-zone pixel ranges too precisely at the margins
edge_cases.mitigation: leave extra margin beyond the estimated safe-zone bounds and check a real test upload on a phone before finalizing, not just the NLE preview

workflow.action: Fix the pacing baseline and the shot-count budget for the target duration
workflow.description: State the cinema ASL trend and retention economics, then derive the 3-5/6-9 shot budget for a 15s/30s target
workflow.gate: the ASL trend, the 3-second drop-off claim, and the duration-to-shot-count arithmetic are all stated

workflow.action: Decide the opening hook and design it for sound-off consumption
workflow.description: Select the single strongest image with no intro frame and confirm it reads on picture alone
workflow.gate: the hook is confirmed strongest-first with no intro frame and passes a sound-off legibility check

workflow.action: Plan the shot-size sequence and the 5-shot luxury skeleton
workflow.description: Assign each planned still/clip a role (hook, establish, action, detail/reaction, wide/loop-CTA) per the wide-medium-close and Murch eye-trace logic
workflow.gate: every planned shot has an assigned skeleton role and adjacent roles differ meaningfully in size/angle

workflow.action: Mark the track's beats and modulate clip lengths around the structural peak
workflow.description: Tap-mark or waveform-mark the track, conform major cuts to downbeats, and set the accelerate/decelerate length curve
workflow.gate: major cuts land on downbeats not every beat, and clip lengths accelerate into and decelerate out of the structural peak

workflow.action: Build sound bridges across the beat-locked cuts
workflow.description: Lead incoming SFX 8-15 frames before picture (J-cut) or trail a music swell over the next clip's opening frames (L-cut)
workflow.gate: every planned bridge point has a J-cut or L-cut offset within the 8-15 frame practice range

workflow.action: Apply speed ramps within the fps-safe range and prep whip-blur bridging
workflow.description: Ramp hero moments with a keyframed speed curve, staying above the ~50-60% floor for AI-clip smoothness
workflow.gate: no ramp pushes an AI clip's slow-motion segment below the artifact-risk threshold without an artifact check

workflow.action: Match motion vectors and execute the chosen transition technique at each cut
workflow.description: Check vector, velocity, screen-region and luminance at each transition cut, then execute the whip-blur, masked-wipe, or flash/invisible-cut recipe selected for that beat
workflow.gate: each transition cut passes the four-point checklist before the specific technique is applied

workflow.action: Select from the full transition inventory and default to the hard-cut workhorse
workflow.description: Confirm the hard-cut-on-beat default is used across most of the reel, reserving the higher-effort techniques for structural beats
workflow.gate: the higher-effort techniques (whip, wipe, flash, match cut) are used only at the reel's structural beats, not throughout

workflow.action: Verify the transition material handoff and reject any failed boundary pair
workflow.description: Confirm every boundary-frame pair passed the upstream QC gate before use; escalate any failure for stills-stage regeneration
workflow.gate: no cut uses a boundary pair that failed upstream QC without having been sent back for regeneration

workflow.action: Trim or design the loop point if the reel closes on a loop
workflow.description: Zoom and trim the boundary frames to a pixel match, or apply the duplicate-tail-plus-cross-dissolve fallback, and confirm the caption loops the sentence too
workflow.gate: the loop point is confirmed only on a reel designed for rewatch value, and the caption/voice line reads continuously across the restart

workflow.action: Assemble the mobile-then-desktop pipeline into the final rising-energy reel within safe-zone framing
workflow.description: Run the beat-locked, transition-executed, budget-compliant cut through the mobile-beat-lock/desktop-finish pipeline, verify safe-zone framing throughout, and confirm the energy curve actually rises toward a peak
workflow.gate: the assembled reel stays inside the shot-count budget, uses only QC'd transition material, keeps every cut inside the safe-zone framing, and demonstrably rises in energy toward a peak before handoff to color grading

priority_rationale: The pacing foundations (ASL/retention economics, the hook rule, and the shot-count budget) come first because every later sequencing, transition and assembly decision is sized and motivated against that shared baseline; the sequencing-logic nodes (shot-size rhythm, Murch's priority ranking, the five-shot skeleton) come next because they define what fills each budgeted slot and how conflicts between rules are resolved; the sound-bridge, speed-ramp and loop techniques then supply the connective craft that operates on top of that sequence; the transition-execution nodes (motion-vector matching, whip-blur, masked wipe, flash/invisible cut, the full inventory, and the material-handoff discipline) come after because they depend on the sequencing and speed-ramp groundwork and govern how each cut is actually built; the tool-form nodes (sound-off design, mobile safe-zone framing, the mobile/desktop hybrid pipeline) come next because they are cross-cutting constraints every cut must satisfy; and the escalation-energy assembly comes last because it composes every upstream node into the single rising-energy reel that is handed off to color grading.

dominance_rules.rule: Retention front-loading dominates classic wide-establishing-first coverage order
dominance_rules.rationale: a sub-15-second reel loses up to half its viewers in the first 3 seconds, so the strongest image must open regardless of classic coverage convention
dominance_rules.trigger: the opening shot choice is being decided for a reel under ~15-30s
dominance_rules.action: open on the single strongest image with no intro frame, establishing geography second per the five-shot skeleton

dominance_rules.rule: Murch's emotion-first priority dominates a strict beat-lock when the two conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: the Rule of Six ranks rhythm at only 10% against emotion's 51%, so a perfectly on-beat cut that lands off the emotional peak is still the wrong cut
dominance_rules.trigger: a beat-locked cut point would land away from the shot's emotional peak
dominance_rules.action: slip the cut by a frame or two toward the nearest strong beat rather than sacrificing the emotional moment

dominance_rules.rule: The photosensitivity/strobing ceiling dominates flash-frame energy regardless of how many structural beats seem to call for one
dominance_rules.rationale: rapid full-frame flashing is an accessibility risk and reads as strobing past roughly two inserts per reel
dominance_rules.trigger: more than two flash-frame moments are being planned for a single reel
dominance_rules.action: cap flash-frame inserts at two per reel and reserve them for the single highest-energy structural beat

dominance_rules.rule: Stills-stage regeneration dominates an editing-side patch for a failed boundary-frame pair
dominance_rules.rationale: stills are the cheap place to fail on a credit-based generation platform; video generation and editing time are the expensive place
dominance_rules.trigger: a boundary-frame pair fails the upstream shot-analysis QC gate
dominance_rules.action: reject the pair back for regeneration before video generation rather than disguising the failure with extra blur, crop, or a flash frame

dominance_rules.rule: Motion-vector agreement dominates any blur or occlusion trick meant to disguise a mismatched cut
dominance_rules.rationale: synthetic blur or a masked wipe only disguises a seam whose underlying vector and velocity already roughly agree; it cannot fix an actual mismatch
dominance_rules.trigger: a whip-blur or masked-wipe technique is about to be applied to a cut
dominance_rules.action: verify the four-point motion-vector checklist first and only then apply the blur/occlusion technique

dominance_rules.rule: The shot-count budget ceiling dominates a per-reel urge to add one more clip
dominance_rules.rationale: padding to the top of the budget purely to fill it trades against the retention economics that set the budget in the first place
dominance_rules.trigger: a reel is being planned or reviewed for its shot count against the duration-based ceiling
dominance_rules.action: spend the budget deliberately; ship at the low end of the range when that is all the strong material supports

dominance_rules.rule: A rewatch-designed intent dominates a default loop ending
dominance_rules.rationale: a full loop wants a decelerating, unnoticed restart while a hard-escalation reel wants energy sustained through the last frame; the two cannot both be maximized
dominance_rules.trigger: a reel's ending is being decided between a loop and a hard escalation peak
dominance_rules.action: use a full loop ending only when the reel is explicitly designed for rewatch value; otherwise loop only the arrival moment or skip the loop entirely

dominance_rules.rule: The sound-off-first hook constraint dominates an audio-dependent opening
dominance_rules.rationale: a significant share of consumption happens sound-off at first touch, so an audio-only hook fails for that share of viewers regardless of its quality with sound on
dominance_rules.trigger: the opening hook relies on a voiceover line, a sound cue, or a caption timed after the visual moment
dominance_rules.action: redesign the hook to read on picture alone first, then layer the audio cue on top for viewers with sound on

anti_rework_rules.rule: Derive the shot-count budget from the target duration before generating any clips
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating an arbitrary number of clips and discovering afterward the reel runs far over or under the intended length

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the opening hook reads on picture alone before finalizing any audio design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building an audio-dependent hook that has to be redesigned once the sound-off-first consumption reality is checked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the four-point motion-vector checklist before applying any blur, wipe, or flash technique to a cut
anti_rework_rules.prevents: disguising a fundamentally mismatched cut with an expensive post technique that still fails, forcing a redo of both the technique and the underlying match

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a boundary-frame pair against the upstream QC gate before it enters the editing timeline
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a failed pair only after editing time has been spent on it, and having to redo the edit once the pair is regenerated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check an AI clip's safe speed-ramp floor before committing a slow-motion keyframe pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ramping past the artifact threshold and having to redo the entire ramp once morphing is spotted in review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide loop-vs-hard-escalation intent before designing the reel's ending
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cutting a decelerating loop ending onto a reel that was supposed to escalate, and having to re-cut the whole back half

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cap flash-frame insert planning at two per reel from the first assembly pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: assembling a reel with flash frames at every structural beat and having to strip most of them out after a strobing complaint

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assemble on mobile only for beat-marking, then move to a desktop NLE before any frame-accurate technique
anti_rework_rules.prevents: attempting single-frame loop trims or motion-vector nudges inside a mobile editor's limited controls and having to redo the work on desktop anyway

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reel is found to pass every individual craft checklist item (budget, transitions, framing) but still feels flat overall
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the shot-length modulation and beat-lock plan specifically for whether the energy curve actually rises toward a peak, not just whether each rule was individually satisfied

iteration_protocol.trigger: a batch shows a specific AI model's clips morphing when ramped below the assumed ~50-60% speed floor
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the safe-ramp floor for that model and flag the finding for the MCP-surface file to confirm the model's actual generated fps

iteration_protocol.trigger: an editor is found papering over a failed boundary-frame pair with an editing trick instead of escalating for regeneration
iteration_protocol.action: reject the affected cuts back to the stills stage, re-flag the handoff discipline, and re-audit recent reels for the same pattern

iteration_protocol.trigger: a published reel is found with a caption or persona face actually covered or cropped by the mobile UI overlay or a platform crop
iteration_protocol.action: widen the safe-zone margins used in assembly beyond the current estimate and re-check recent reels for the same exposure

iteration_protocol.trigger: an official Meta/Instagram safe-zone pixel spec or sound-off consumption statistic becomes fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimated ranges and the no-percentage-claimed caveat with the confirmed figures

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reel is found to exceed the two-flash-frame cap or otherwise read as strobing in review
iteration_protocol.action: strip the excess flash-frame inserts back to the cap and re-verify the remaining insert sits on the single highest-energy beat

iteration_protocol.trigger: the sibling cover/shot-analysis KB changes its frame-pairing rules or QC rubric criteria
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the transition-material handoff contract and the transition-inventory selection logic against the updated upstream criteria
